steps.body: Import/open the repository in Code when you want edits, commands, commits, pushes, or PR creation. A Chat explanation does not change the remote repository.

lessons.outcome: You have an answer grounded in accessible GitHub content without needing a local checkout for reading.
limits: Chat’s GitHub-reading tools cannot post comments, create/edit issues, merge, push, or change remote data.
Private access still requires the connected account’s permissions. Code search and some API endpoints may need authentication even for public repositories.

fixes.problem: A public link cannot be read
fixes.solution: Check the URL/version, API permissions and rate limits. Use the browser/source page when the GitHub API cannot serve that content.

lessons.example: Read this GitHub pull request and explain the change, the files involved, and what still needs testing. Link to the evidence you used.

lessons.title: Work with local Git branches
lessons.summary: Keep file edits, commits, and conversation forks distinct.
lessons.location: Code in a Git repository workspace; Terminal for direct Git commands.
before: Have Git tools ready and select the repository-root workspace.
Review uncommitted changes before switching branches.

steps.title: Inspect the repository first
steps.body: Ask Code for Git status, current/all branches, diff, and recent log. Read the result before changing branch state.

steps.title: Create and switch deliberately
steps.body: Ask for a named feature branch if needed. Creating a branch and checking it out are separate operations in the app’s Git tools; confirm the current branch afterward.

steps.title: Review and commit the intended paths
steps.body: Inspect the diff and include only the changes you want in the commit. A local commit records work on this branch; it does not publish it by itself.

steps.title: Pull or push with review
steps.body: Use the supported Git operations or Commit & push. If the remote branch has changed or a conflict appears, inspect and resolve it before retrying publication.

lessons.outcome: Your repository is on the intended branch with a reviewable local history and known publication state.
limits: Forking a conversation does not create a Git branch or separate copy of the project.
Deleting a branch, forcing operations, switching with local changes, or resolving conflicts can affect work. Read the action/approval and keep important work recoverable.

fixes.solution: Inspect status and the exact Git error. Save/commit the intended local work or resolve the stated conflict rather than discarding it to make a command pass.

lessons.title: Share something into AndroidHarness
lessons.summary: Bring text, links, and supported attachments from another app into a Chat.
lessons.location: Another Android app → Share → AndroidHarness.
before: The source app must offer Android sharing for the content.
Review private content and the model destination before sending.

steps.title: Choose AndroidHarness in Share
steps.body: Use the source app’s Android share sheet. AndroidHarness opens a review sheet for the shared text and supported attachment previews.

steps.title: Choose the conversation
steps.body: Use New Chat or pick an existing regular Chat. Search the destination list when you have many conversations.

steps.title: Add the question
steps.body: Type what you want done, or use a suggestion such as summarize, explain, translate, or check. Review the content before using the open action.

steps.title: Continue in the prepared Chat
steps.body: Check the destination, attachments, and selected model. Complete the request in the conversation using the normal message controls.

lessons.outcome: The shared content is prepared in the regular Chat you selected.
limits: The share destination list is for regular Chat sessions; it does not directly run a project-editing task in Code.
Attachment permissions, readable formats, size limits, and model vision support still apply. Sharing a link does not guarantee the page can be read.

fixes.solution: Return to the source app and share it again, or save a supported copy and attach it from the Chat picker.
